Because deep RL optimizes expected return without explicit safety constraints, most applications have been confined to simulated settings or highly controlled real‑world domains where failures are tolerable.  

To mitigate the safety and stability shortcomings of RL, a number of research directions have emerged. One line of work integrates control‑theoretic concepts, especially robust control, with the expressive power of neural‑network policies. Examples include methods that jointly learn Lyapunov functions and control policies to enforce stochastic stability, and approaches that cast continuous‑time control synthesis as min‑max differential games in which the controller and disturbance play opposing roles.
